newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF mission to return to Moscow next week.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to return to Moscow next week.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission will leave Moscow on Monday without taking a decision on whether Russia should receive the latest tranche of its $10 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility, but will return early next week for further discussions, a senior Russian source said.

The mission, which had already left Moscow once last month without taking a decision on the tranche of about $340 million, will probably be able to come to a decision after its return, said the source, a member of the Russian side in the talks.
"Judging by everything, the decision will be positive for us," he told Reuters.
A decision could be formally announced when the IMF board meets in the second week of December, he said.
The mission had originally been scheduled to leave last Friday, but extended its stay to Monday. It will now return after the U.S. Thanksgiving Day break at the end of this week.
The mission had a final set of talks on Monday with Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits and First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin, the source said.
"The members of the mission are going back to the U.S. for the holidays and then they will return for a final decision," he said.

The mission failed to reach agreement last month with Russia mainly over the question of tax shortfalls. The IMF made it clear that it wanted to see an improvement in tax revenues before disbursing the next tranche.
Tax collection has improved in the last two months, but the IMF wants evidence that the improvement is sustainable, sources close to the talks said.
